items.title: Miyazaki suggests FromSoftware is keen to return to single-player games after The Duskbloods and Elden Ring: Nightreign
items.summary: Souls house FromSoftware has done back-to-back multiplayer games with The Duskbloods and Elden Ring: Nightreign. But it hasn't forgotten solo players.
items.content:
Image credit: Eurogamer/FromSoftware News by Robert Purchese Associate Editor Published on Aug. 20, 2026, 4:44 p.m. 2 comments Follow The Duskbloods Hidetaka Miyazaki , the president of FromSoftware and director of so many revered Soulsian games, has suggested the studio is keen to return to making single-player games after The Duskbloods.

Speaking to IGN , Miyazaki explained it was a coincidence that 2025's Elden Ring: Nightreign and The Duskbloods were both multiplayer games. "It's funny because there was never really any big plan that these two games [Nightreign and The Duskbloods] would both release next to each other," he said.

"I mean, that's a different director," he added, referring to Junya Ishizaki who helmed Nightreign, "but both of those ideas just coincided with being multiplayer games. It's not necessarily some big reveal saying that this is the direction we plan to go moving forward. We still have a heavy focus on single-player content as well. This is just something that happened to work out the way it did."

It was while continuing this thought, and saying it had been fun to make a multiplayer game, that Miyazaki said: "But it's like, the more you work on something multiplayer for a long time, if anything, it scratches that itch only to want to make something single-player again."

FromSoftware's last big single-player game was 2022's barnstorming Elden Ring , which included a more traditional form of multiplayer for the studio - including co-op and invasions. But Elden Ring didn't showcase multiplayer in the way Nightreign did or that Switch 2 exclusive The Duskbloods will - with a much more actively competitive multiplayer PvPvE experience.

Indeed, it seems as though it's The Duskbloods that's the anomaly for FromSoftware, with Miyazaki describing it as an outlet for ideas that "didn't really fit in the context of a single-player game".

"Over time," he said, "a lot of those ideas piled up, things that you wish you could have done here and there. Having an outlet for them, somewhere we can find a place where they all fit, or can be made to fit specifically in that multiplayer context, is something that was always at the forefront of my mind."

The Duskbloods is a Switch 2 exclusive made in partnership with Nintendo. Miyazaki said this relationship came about from a mixture of Nintendo being "very excited and very receptive to the idea" of The Duskbloods, and "very forward thinking in terms of how to do it". Nintendo's input can be felt in the game, as well, particularly in how it helps ease players in..

"The onboarding tutorials and making sure players understand how the game works and how to succeed in the game is something we've historically not been super great at conveying instantly," Miyazaki said. "We've definitely just dropped players in and hoped they would figure it out. In this case, Nintendo is definitely the right partner for better conveying that information in a way that is understandable to the player; it definitely suits their strengths."

This weekend's The Duskbloods network test runs in five phases , one each day from 21st August (Friday) through to 24th August (Monday). The full game has no release date yet, despite a 24th September date appearing briefly today , but FromSoftware has previously committed to it coming out this year . The pertinent question this autumn is: how close to GTA 6 's 19th November release dare it go?

items.title: FromSoftware Boss Miyazaki Says, 'We Still Have a Heavy Focus on Single-Player Content'
items.summary: While Elden Ring: Nightreign and The Duskbloods are back-to-back multiplayer games, FromSoftware's Miyazaki says they're still focused on single-player content.
items.content:
Developer FromSoftware is gearing up for The Duskbloods with a network test and a recent hands-on preview that I got to take part in. Coming off of its most recent game Elden Ring: Nightreign , which is a co-operative multiplayer experience, and now the upcoming PvPvE with The Duskbloods, you might be wondering if the studio has another single-player game lined up. Rest assured, FromSoft isn't putting all its eggs into the multiplayer basket.

As part of an interview I had with FromSoftware president and The Duskbloods director Hidetaka Miyazaki , I asked if doing back-to-back multiplayer games was indicative of the direction the team is going. He reassured us that FromSoftware is not done making single-player games.

"It's not necessarily some big reveal saying this is the direction we plan to go in moving forward. We still have a heavy focus on single-player content as well. This is just something that happened to work out the way it did," Miyazaki told me. "It's funny because there was never really any big plan that these two games would both release next to each other."

He explained that he and the team have had a lot ideas pile up over the years and he saw The Duskbloods, which is heavily influenced by board games and TTRPGs when it comes to gameplay mechanics, as an opportunity to try those out. "These things seemed like great ideas but didn't really fit the context of a single-player game," Miyazaki explained.

Miyazaki talked about how this is the kind of game he wants to see exist and made something he himself would want to play. "Personally, it's very fun to make a multiplayer game like this. It's not something we've done a lot and we're looking forward to seeing players' reactions and getting feedback," he said.

He concluded by telling me, "If anything, it's like the more you work on something multiplayer for a long time it scratches that itch only to want to make something single-player again."

The future of FromSoftware and the question of whether it will release a sequel to Elden Ring or Bloodborne is a hot topic, after the boss of parent company Kadokawa survived a recent shareholder vote on his future amid increasing pressure from an activist investor who believes the company has failed to capitalize on Elden Ring’s enormous success. The 30 million-selling Elden Ring launched in 2022, and since then FromSoftware has released expansion Shadow of the Erdtree (2024) and multiplayer spinoff, Elden Ring: Nightreign (2025).

In June, Miyazaki commented on the shareholder pressure Kadokawa was under . Reassuring fans, he insisted that FromSoftware can still “freely make the kind of games we want to make without excessive interference." Could Elden Ring 2 be on the cards? In December 2024, Miyazaki said FromSoftware was not considering making Elden Ring 2 , but wouldn't shut down the possibility in the future. If not, there is an Elden Ring movie in the works.

Be sure to read my full interview with Miyazaki where we talk about partnering with Nintendo, future plans for The Duskbloods, and more. And check out my hands-on preview of The Duskbloods after playing it for eight hours.

Michael Higham is an editor at IGN who regularly contributes with reviews, previews, features, and news in written and video form. He's usually entrusted with covering long RPGs and tech products, but he's got range when it comes to games. You'll also catch him at events and hosting video content, including IGN's weekly podcast Unlocked .

items.title: 'Elden Ring Meets Settlers of Catan' Revealed as Switch 2's Next Multiplayer Swing
items.summary: What is The Duskbloods? We explain FromSoftware's Elden Ring successor.
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Michael McWhertor Published Aug 20, 2026, 10:00 AM EDT Previews The Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive is an odd but compelling mix of gameplay styles

Image: FromSoftware/Nintendo Jump Links OK, so what is The Duskbloods? How matches work in The Duskbloods Kith and kin (and zeppelins) If you've played a FromSoftware " Soulslike " during the past decade and a half, you probably know what to expect from the developer's games: white-knuckle combat, challenging and grotesque monsters, and inventive online interactions with other players both friendly and adversarial. FromSoftware's next game, The Duskbloods , will feel familiar in that sense. In it, players take on the role of supernatural beings known as Bloodsworn who hunt grisly creatures. Players will do so with the aid — and interference — of other players in online play.

Unlike Dark Souls and Elden Ring , The Duskbloods focuses less on players charging forward against challenging odds, dying repeatedly, and charging forward again. It is instead a match-based multiplayer game in which eight players fight to earn victory points called Virtue, following multiple possible pathways to victory.

Game director Hidetaka Miyazaki says he hopes The Duskbloods ' game design leads to "unexpected drama."

FromSoftware has described The Duskbloods as a PvPvE game. That's accurate, in that there are player-versus-player moments, including each match's final contest. But much of the game can be played fighting against the environment, and rarely facing off against other players. During a hands-on gameplay preview at FromSoftware's headquarters in Tokyo, I focused as much as I could on the PvE aspects of The Duskbloods , slaying hordes of creatures, powering up my character, and collecting items from the environment.

My strategy was successful enough that I ultimately won five of the matches we played as a group. But some matches were a total bust, and the PvP-focused players were victorious.

Image: FromSoftware/Nintendo In The Duskbloods , players choose a prebuilt character called a Bloodsworn. The pre-built nature of the characters is similar to those of Elden Ring Nightreign . Each has a close-range melee weapon and a long-range attack, and all characters have unique special abilities and superpowers, some of which unlock over the course of a match.

Bloodsworn all share one thing in common: They're all good at jumping, making them capable of easily navigating the highly vertical environments of The Duskbloods ' maps. Characters can triple jump, air dash, and perform a Superman-like leap to scale buildings, hop onto bridges, or cross vast chasms.

Bloodsworn have another ability in common. They can "Howl" to stagger enemies, similar to the stunning effect of Bloodborne 's firearms. Bloodsworn can then "Drink Blood" from a staggered foe to refill their health and spellbind certain foes to make them temporary allies.

Image: FromSoftware/Nintendo In FromSoftware's upcoming network test for The Duskbloods , six Bloodsworn are playable. More are expected for the game's 2026 launch on Nintendo Switch 2. The current list of Bloodsworn includes easy-to-grasp characters like Albert, who fights with a sword, submachine gun, and whips of blood, and weirdos like Zork, a man in a metal diving suit who uses a length of undersea cable and a speargun to fight. Zork can also take off like a rocket ship, thanks to his built-in jetpack.

Players of past FromSoftware games will find some analogs in the Bloodsworn cast. Chakram user Trang Lanh fights like Nightreign 's Duchess, while Zork is a classic Dark Souls "fat roll" type of fighter. But FromSoftware clearly isn't afraid to get weird with the playable roster: One character unlocks the ability to transform into a hungry dinosaur as he levels up.

Image: FromSoftware/Nintendo Matches of The Duskbloods , known as Dusk Battles, require eight players, based on the network test build I played. Each match can be played solo or in duos, and matches last roughly 25-30 minutes. Players matchmake into a game and are transported to one of the game's maps. I played exclusively on Lawanro City, a Victorian city that features a handful of key landmarks: a giant clock tower, an underground sewer system, a large cathedral, and a shallow lake. Forests, caves, and bridges flesh out the map.

Players can choose which sector of the map they want to spawn into, both at the start of the game and after dying. There's little to no penalty for dying, though it takes you out of the game for a moment and other players may benefit from your death.

Once on the map, your mission is explicit: earn Virtue. These points are akin to victory points in tabletop games, as The Duskbloods ' design was directly influenced by games like The Settlers of Catan , in which players have multiple avenues to victory.

items.title: FromSoftware can do anything
items.summary: The ‘Soulslike’ studio is always trying new ideas.

The Elden Ring studio continues to chart new paths through games like The Duskbloods.

Andrew Webster Close Andrew Webster Senior entertainment editor Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Share Gift Image: Nintendo Andrew Webster Close Andrew Webster Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

There’s something just a little bit different about FromSoftware’s office in Tokyo. Like with any other successful video game studio, there’s extensive security to get in the door, a minimalist lobby with framed posters from the studio’s most recent releases, and a large glass display case filled with statues from ceremonies ranging from the BAFTAs to The Game Awards. But the hallways are painted black, a fitting theme for a developer known for crafting dark, gothic worlds and a hint at what new creations are lurking inside.

While it has largely become known for a singular style of action game — dubbed “Soulslike,” after the massively influential Dark Souls series — FromSoft has steadily continued to try new things, pushing its signature style into new genres. Perhaps the most extreme example of this is the studio’s next release: The Duskbloods , a competitive multiplayer game set in a world of vampires that will be exclusive to the Switch 2 and published by Nintendo when it launches later this year. It’s a new genre, new setting, new platform, and new publisher all rolled into one game. But after Elden Ring , which has sold more than 30 million copies since it launched in 2022 , the team at FromSoft now also feels more assured in expanding their horizons.

“With the success of Elden Ring , as a company it has definitely allowed us to explore, I wouldn’t say risky ideas, but things that we might not have had the confidence for,” FromSoftware president Hidetaka Miyazaki, who also directed both Elden Ring and The Duskbloods , told me during a recent hands-on event at the studio’s office.

The studio’s rise to this point has been slow and steady. FromSoft’s first release was the dungeon crawling RPG King’s Field in 1994, and while it launched a consistent stream of titles after that — including the cult-hit mech battling Armored Core series — it was more than a decade later when the studio really started making its mark with the release of Demon’s Souls in 2009. Directed by Miyazaki, the game thrust players into a harsh fantasy world, one where death was a constant and the combat was punishing. It was an experience that demanded a lot from players, but also rewarded their patience with thrilling victories and a story that gradually revealed itself.

It was an unlikely hit that spawned a new genre of action games, and was followed up by a number of successors, including a trilogy of Dark Souls titles and the Victorian-era-inspired Bloodborne in 2015 . Those games were all successes, selling millions of copies, but it wasn’t until Elden Ring that the studio had its first blockbuster hit. The game not only sold well, but spawned a large-scale expansion, a co-op spinoff called Nightreign , and an upcoming film adaptation from A24 and director Alex Garland. Part of what made Elden Ring a hit was that it took what FromSoft had become known for — relentless action, subtle storytelling, and immersive worlds — and translated it into an open-world adventure and gave players more freedom to explore its bleak and beautiful fantastical realm.

Even with its signature game style cemented, FromSoft was continuously experimenting. Sandwiched in between the launches of Dark Souls 3 (2016) and Elden Ring (2022) were a pair of one-off games — a solemn VR story called Déraciné in 2018, and a ninja action game called Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice a year later — that showed the studio expanding its range. At the time, Miyazaki, who directed both games, explained FromSoft’s approach to taking on new projects.

“I think one of the studio’s characteristics is to embrace wholeheartedly what we feel is interesting; what we perceive to be worthwhile, cool, or beautiful; and to place these ideals at the foundation of the games we make,” he told me in 2019 . “Part of those things we feel may deviate slightly from what is considered to have mass appeal. This ‘unorthodox’ nature could well be what ties our games and our culture together.”

The Duskbloods may seem like a big departure, but it also fits neatly into this philosophy. Over the years, FromSoft had steadily been injecting multiplayer elements into its largely single-player games; in Elden Ring , for instance, you can summon other players to help you in battle. As the studio experimented in this realm, a number of multiplayer-centric ideas were filed away. “There are a lot of ideas that we had wanted to try that didn’t necessarily fit in that context of a single-player game,” Miyazaki said during the Duskbloods preview in Tokyo. “Those pile up over the years.” That eventually culminated into The Duskbloods .

items.title: We played The Duskbloods, the Switch 2’s wildest new exclusive
items.content:
Entertainment Close Entertainment Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Hands-on with the upcoming multiplayer vampire game from Elden Ring studio FromSoftware.

Andrew Webster Close Andrew Webster Senior entertainment editor Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Share Gift Image: Nintendo Entertainment Close Entertainment Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Share Gift Andrew Webster Close Andrew Webster Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

The Duskbloods is a world away from the approachable games Nintendo is known for. But for its next Switch 2 exclusive, the company has partnered with Elden Ring developer FromSoftware on a hardcore multiplayer game about vampires. And after spending a few hours playing through its gothic world at FromSoft’s offices in Tokyo, I’m convinced that The Duskbloods could end up being one of the most important exclusives for Nintendo’s latest console.

It’s a notable change for the company. People buy Nintendo consoles for Nintendo games. That’s a generally accepted truth, and also one that’s backed up by data — a quick glance at the bestselling games across platforms like the Switch and Nintendo 3DS reveals expected names like Mario Kart , Pokémon , and Animal Crossing . Titles from outside developers can be an integral part of broadening a platform’s appeal, but that’s something that Nintendo has historically struggled with. Which is what makes The Duskbloods so intriguing.

The Duskbloods is not an easy game to describe. In a universe of vampires that spans multiple time periods, eight players, controlling vampiric characters known as the Bloodsworn, descend on a level filled with enemies and gigantic boss creatures. Over the course of several phases the group is whittled down until only a few remain, who must then fight until only one is left. This isn’t a Fortnite -style battle royale, however. Instead, The Duskbloods is designed to mix the thrill of competitive play with the roleplaying fantasy that FromSoft has become known for through games like Dark Souls and Bloodborne .

Key to this is something that the game calls “virtue.” Essentially, it’s a system that allows you accumulate points over the course of a match by doing just about everything. You can get virtue by collecting the most items, or by killing the most minor enemies, or by taking down boss creatures like a gigantic frog with far too many humanlike teeth. There are virtue points for exploration — the levels are littered with hidden corpses you can discover — and in the later rounds you can get a huge burst of virtue points by defeating other players on specific points of the map, or making a pledge at an altar before another player stops you.

Each match is divided into four phases, and the player count slowly shrinks through what’s known as “the culling.” Basically, if you don’t have enough virtue points by the time a round ends then you’re out. How many points you need depends entirely on how much virtue other players have collected. The idea is that, even if you maybe aren’t the best one-on-one fighter, you can still progress through the game and make it to the final phase, since there are so many different ways to earn points. And aside from the final round, you’ll respawn immediately after dying with your virtue intact, which makes it easier to try things and explore without fear of the game ending.

In practice, The Duskbloods can be an overwhelming experience, at least initially. It took me some time to wrap my head around the points system; in most competitive multiplayer games, killing other players is the clearest path to victory. Here, though, that’s not the case, particularly at the beginning. Instead, the early rounds are best spent exploring the map, defeating weaker enemies, and generally strengthening your character by acquiring items and experience.

And there’s a lot more to The Duskbloods ’ complexity than just the points system. For starters, there are multiple vampiric characters to play as, each of whom has a very different playstyle. In the early version of the game I played — which is the same as the network test that will run later in August — there are six characters to choose from. There’s an aging senator who wields a rapier that doubles as a cane, and who can both summon a prehistoric bird as a ranged attack and temporarily transform into a bloodthirsty dinosaur. There’s a ninja with circular blades, a mysterious man who can shoot columns of fire from a stone embedded in his hand, and an armor-clad weirdo named Zork who carries around an electrified chunk of undersea cable.

items.title: Elden Ring Meets Skyrim in New Dark Fantasy Game You Can Play for Free Now
items.summary: No other game mashes Elden Ring and Skyrim as well as Mortal Shell II.
items.content:
Mortal Shell II key art 1 Image via Playstack By Marley Hughes Published Aug 19, 2026, 8:45 PM EDT Marley Hughes owns a library of games through many digital platforms, including Steam, and is steadily building up a physical collection as well, mainly in the case of older video game consoles such as those from Sega. He uses his knowledge from what he's played or heard to bring readers steadfast information about gaming. Sign in to your CBR account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Sometimes the best video games are those that blend aspects of two iconic titles. Just imagining a game that combines elements of Skyrim and Elden Ring together is enough to make a gamer's fingers itchy.

The result is Mortal Shell II , which is currently in open beta on Steam. The game is set to fully release on August 20, 2026, and in the meantime, it's already making a case for itself as one of the best RPGs of the year.

Mortal Shell II action 1 Image via Playstack Saying Mortal Shell II combines the best of Elden Ring and Skyrim is hardly an exaggeration, especially for those who played the first Mortal Shell game. Set in Fallgrim, a cold, grimdark world that doesn't look out of place in either Elden Ring or Skyrim , one of the key differences is that Mortal Shell II's world is considerably less organized.

Players control the Harbinger, a being tasked with restoring Fallgrim. Having fallen from grace in the years since the events of the previous game, it's up to the Harbinger to restore the world to its former glory. This will mean taking on some of the biggest threats that have befallen Fallgrim.

Beyond standard enemies, these threats include bosses like Vrannic the Grand Illusionist and Magdalena the Lady of the Woods. These bosses have their own gimmicks, from Vrannic's ability to conjure projectiles to Magdalena's 360-degree flame attacks. Attacks this powerful can be hard to dodge, especially if they outright surround the player the way Magdalena's fire spell does.

To help persevere through the game, players must collect Shells, which embody the spirit of old powerful warriors. For example, the shell of Harros the Vassal will strengthen players' combat abilities, while Proxima the Broodseeker's shell will improve players' damage output against enemies. These shells have few drawbacks in combat, and they help make for an intense Action RPG romp, especially as the game continues on.

For that matter, Mortal Shell II provides players with a myriad of weapons. They include melee weapons like swords and scythes and long-range weapons like crossbows and naylshottes. These weapons make the game more accessible than Elden Ring or Skyrim .

Mortal Shell II action 2 Image via Playstack The good news for those uncertain if they should play Mortal Shell II is that the game shares the same developer and publisher as the first Mortal Shell game. To elaborate, the game is developed by Cold Symmetry, an indie studio run by industry veterans, and published by Playstack, a well-established indie gaming label based in the United Kingdom.

Aside from the Mortal Shell series, Playstack has had a long track record of putting out some of the most interesting indie titles out there, most notably Balatro , which is one of the best roguelike games of the 2020s . Other upcoming examples include About Fishing and Dice Vaders , along with licensed games like Star Trek: Outposts Unknown .

Of course, it all comes down to Cold Symmetry, which was responsible for the game's development in the first place. The company already did well with the first Mortal Shell game, which sold over one million copies and received generally favorable reviews from critics. Given how refined Mortal Shell II appears compared to the first game, there is no reason to doubt that it is bound to be an even bigger hit.

With higher stakes, an improved shell mechanic, and a greater variety of weapons, Mortal Shell II is likely to outperform the first Mortal Shell game in terms of sales and reviews. As the game remains in public beta until its release on Thursday, August 20, 2026, there is no better time to try out one of the best indie games of the year.

items.title: Elden Ring Gets Promising Gameplay Update on Switch 2 in New Video
items.summary: Nintendo and Bandai Namco show off Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition ahead of release
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Michael McWhertor Published Aug 18, 2026, 1:26 PM EDT News Looks like the Lands Between are going to be OK

Elden Ring movie officially sets release date and unveils cast Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake may be canceled, but the original now plays better than ever Tomb Raider remake gameplay changes have fans conflicted Elden Ring's Switch 2 version looks better than ever in new official gameplay Image: FromSoftware/Bandai Namco Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Sign in to your Polygon.com account 2023's Game of the Year Elden Ring is finally making its way to Nintendo Switch 2 later this month after a substantial delay. The Tarnished Edition of FromSoftware's open-world action-RPG was originally pegged for a 2025 release, but after multiple reports of Elden Ring running poorly on Switch 2 , publisher Bandai Namco gave the port's developers more time to cook.

Fortunately, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition looks like it's shaping up to be great, based on new official gameplay and video of the game running in handheld mode on Switch 2.

A new gameplay showcase video released Tuesday offers both a minute-long primer on what Elden Ring is and some evidence of how the game performs on Nintendo's handheld. For Elden Ring veterans, there's not a lot new here; the video doesn't reveal much more about the Tarnished Edition's new prebuilt starting classes. But for Switch 2 owners just getting their first taste of Elden Ring , it's a simple, straightforward look at what FromSoft's game has to offer, including cooperative multiplayer and a tough-as-nails Soulslike on the go.

In addition to the official, direct-feed gameplay of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition , there's also new video of off-screen gameplay, both in docked and handheld modes. Japanese outlet Denfaminico Gamer has nine minutes of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition running on Switch 2, showing what appears to be a very playable version of the game.

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition has been a long time coming. The Switch 2 port was originally announced in April 2025 at Nintendo's big showcase for its new console. The Elden Ring port was revealed alongside a handful of similar Switch 2 rereleases, including Cyberpunk 2077 , Hogwarts Legacy , Street Fighter 6 , and Hitman World of Assassination .

Originally, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition was slated to arrive in 2025, but after a rough showing at last summer's Gamescom event , developer FromSoftware and Bandai Namco delayed the game into 2026. More recent showings of the Elden Ring Switch 2 port were more promising, however. Now it appears that FromSoftware and Bandai Namco have managed to get the open-world fantasy role-playing game in working order on Nintendo's hybrid console-handheld.

Elden Ring is currently available on PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X. The Switch 2 version is coming on Aug. 28, with the Tarnished Edition bonus content available on other platforms as paid DLC.

Kit Connor, Ben Whishaw, Cailee Spaeny, and Tom Burke will headline Alex Garland's adaptation, hitting IMAX in March 2028

items.title: Elden Ring’s Rough Switch 2 Build Is Gone, As FromSoftware’s Cleanup Signals How Good The Duskbloods Could Run
items.summary: Elden Ring's Nintendo Switch 2 gameplay bodes well for FromSoftware's upcoming Switch 2 exclusive The Duskbloods
items.content:
FromSoftware was originally supposed to launch Elden Ring on Nintendo Switch 2 last year, but the Japanese publisher headed by Hidetaka Miyazaki eventually chose not to compromise on the port's quality, and delay the Tarnished Edition to August 28 . Looking at some new footage, the Japanese developer did make the right call, as it shows a significant improvement over last year's build that bodes extremely well for the upcoming The Duskbloods .

The new Elden Ring Nintendo Switch 2 footage was shared online by Japanese publications such as Famitsu and Denfaminico Gamer , showcasing the game running in both docked and handheld mode. Although it does not hit 60 FPS, the Switch 2 seems to be handling the game much better in docked mode, as the footage shows no stuttering whatsoever, even during the game's intense boss battles. While 30 FPS is not ideal for this type of game, FromSoftware fans had to endure much worse in the past to enjoy a game like Bloodborne , whose frame pacing issues on PlayStation 4 had a significant impact on the experience.

In handheld mode, Elden Ring does seem to fare reasonably well, although the footage does show some frame rate drops during boss battles. As we are still 10 days from release, there's the chance that these could be smoothed out ahead of release.

Although FromSoftware has developed some of the best action RPGs of the past few years, it is undeniable how, in terms of tech, the Japanese studio is far from being the most advanced, as its games usually have some issues that are not always ironed out, such as the aforementioned Bloodborne and even Elden Ring itself at launch on PC and consoles, or require modding on PC to bring the best out of them, such as with the Dark Souls 3 path tracing mod.

As such, looking at the significant improvement of Elden Ring on Nintendo Switch 2 , there's plenty of reasons to be optimistic about The Duskbloods , the studio's next game launching later this year as a Switch 2 exclusive. Since FromSoftware uses its own proprietary engine for its games, any advancement and optimization made for Elden Ring is likely to have a positive impact on the new game, which is set to deliver a rather unique experience, compared to the studio's other single-player games.

The August 28th Elden Ring Tarnished Edition release date is fast approaching. FromSoftware developers are running out of time to optimize the Switch 2 game . After a delay to tweak performance , new videos show more consistent visuals on the Nintendo system. Still, borderline 30 fps graphics may not persuade buyers worried about the high price tag .

Japanese gaming site Famitsu generally praised how the Souls game transitioned to the portable console. Although the magazine cautions the build isn’t final, YouTube footage provides a glimpse at docked and handheld modes.

When connected to a TV, the Elden Ring Switch 2 port appears to render at 30 fps, possibly reaching a higher mark at times. Unlike earlier videos , there is no apparent stuttering upon entering open-world areas. Combat also seems responsive, even lacking the 60 fps performance option available on the PS5 and Xbox Series X.

Handheld mode has always been the larger concern, with the GPU and CPU somewhat throttled. The Famitsu tester was able to “play smoothly without any particular discomfort.” In the YouTube clip, the graphics largely maintain the same targets as when docked. However, other recent leaked recordings expose frame rate drops in intense boss fights.

Whether gamers approve of the Elden Ring Tarnished Edition may hinge on expectations. Even on the PS5 and Series X consoles, the FromSoftware title struggles to hold 60 fps. A closer comparison is the Steam Deck , where, after numerous updates, developers optimized the game for Valve’s hardware. At 1280 × 800 and reasonable detail settings, frame rates now meet the 30 fps benchmark.

Another obstacle for wavering Switch 2 owners is cost. The action RPG demands $79.99, and its Game-Key Card format requires a large download. Also, the Tarnished Pack with two new starting classes, armor, and weapons will arrive on other platforms for $4.99.

With the Elden Ring Switch 2 release date imminent, the industry will soon learn if the performance gains are enough to convince skeptics.

items.title: Mortal Shell 2 review - falls short of Elden Ring's greatness
items.summary: Our Mortal Shell 2 review looks at the game
items.content:
Our Mortal Shell 2 review looks at the game's open world, boss fights, and combat, and whether it can hold a candle to Elden Ring.

Mortal Shell 2 clearly tries to imitate the success of Elden Ring's open world, yet falls drastically short, with a map that can be frustrating to navigate. However, the combat and shell system are where the game shines, offering an enjoyable experience that's sure to give you that Soulslike thrill.

I knew that Mortal Shell 2 was going to be a brutal experience - I'd be foolish to head into a Soulslike thinking otherwise - but the opening hour shows just how challenging it is, and that's before you even get to the action RPG's open world. Set in a dark-fantasy world, Cold Symmetry's sequel expands its setting to a world of interconnected areas, to mixed effect.

You are the Harbinger, a being on a quest to collect the missing eggs (known as ovum) and return them to Marrow Keep, and to do so, you need to find and equip different shells. Each one comes with its own unlockable skills and benefits, and it's up to you to track them down out in the world along with the ovum. Shells form the base of your build, something you learn very early on. However, each of these shells was a real person, which leads me to one of my favorite things about the game: exploring the characters' history. Each one has a deep backstory, and the more you explore, the deeper your bond and efficiency with the shell becomes. It's a mechanic that helps MS2 stand apart from other games in the soulslike genre.

Much like Elden Ring, Mortal Shell 2 features an open world that beckons you to explore as you search for ovum to bring back to Marrow Keep. As a similarly dark, fantasy-based action RPG like FromSoftware's masterpiece, the Mortal Shell sequel also provides you with a base of operations, akin to Roundtable Hold or Firelink Shrine in Elden Ring.

While there is plenty to explore, with plenty of dungeons lurking in the darkness, I can't help but think that the world feels a little hollow, and I found exploring it to be rather frustrating from the offset. I don't expect to be spoon-fed, but a little bit of direction beyond 'here's two shells' would be nice, along with a clearer indication of where I'll find map fragments. I can't help but draw the obvious comparison to Elden Ring's The Lands Between map, where not only do I feel rewarded for my exploration, but it's a joy to do so and is rarely confusing as to where you need to go.

For its open world shortcomings, I have to complement Mortal Shell 2's boss fights. Not only do they pose a real challenge, but they're fun to overcome, giving that distinct sense of accomplishment I enjoy from these games. There are plenty to encounter, some even waiting for you in the open world, just like Elden Ring. I know I keep drawing the comparison, but it's very clearly the inspiration behind some of the creative decisions in Mortal Shell 2, and that includes the bosses.

While the combat feels somewhat clunky at times, it's also one of the game's biggest strengths, with each shell you find offering an assortment of items to alter your skills. It offers you a bit more freedom than other soulslikes, as instead of leveling up individual stats, you increase all the Harbinger's attributes in one go, and select what upgrades you want for each shell. It means I get to switch between playstyles and weapons easily.

One thing I'm a fan of in games is quality accessibility options. I love a brutal challenge, but Soulslikes are also narratively interesting, and it's a shame that some people don't get to experience them due to the gameplay difficulty. Mortal Shell 2 attempts to make your time easier if you so choose with the Slayer seal, but enemies still pose a challenge, enough so that I'd say it does little to truly make a difference. It falls short, whereas a game like Lies of P excels by offering an easy difficulty setting instead of a mere item, which doesn't actually hinder your enemies. I had an easier time using a seal that enables parrying.

I played the game on the Steam Machine, so if you want to play Mortal Shell 2 on Valve's new hardware, I have great news: it performs really well on its base settings, with minimal issues. However, I advise against high settings, as it had my game chugging along at a very pitiful fps. I also encountered an issue where my gloom would be waiting for me out of bounds after death, leaving me no way of getting them back - which is a pretty big deal, considering how important leveling up is in this game. Luckily, a day one patch is on the way, so I suspect this won't remain an issue.

All in all, Mortal Shell 2 is okay - it fills the Soulslike void and does encompass everything you need in an action-RPG. The combat is fun, the bosses are interesting, and the shell system is intuitive, but I can't stop thinking about returning to Elden Ring instead.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.
